issues.legal_issue: A successor to a widow-landlord must follow the statutory process and time limit for terminating a tenant’s lease to recover land for personal cultivation, notwithstanding that the widow was deemed to cultivate land personally while leasing it.
material_facts: The adopted son had granted his stepmother a life interest in land for maintenance, and she leased the land to the tenant.
After the widow died, her successor sought possession from the tenant but gave no notice terminating the tenancy and made no application to the tenancy authority.
The suit for possession was resisted on the ground that the tenant was protected under the tenancy legislation, and the courts below accepted that defence.
issues.conclusion: The successor’s failure to give the required notice and make the required application within the applicable period meant that the suit for possession was rightly dismissed; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(6), Explanation 1, a widow could be deemed to cultivate land personally even when it was cultivated through tenants; Sections 2(18) and 4 defined tenants and persons deemed to be tenants. Under Section 31, a landlord seeking to terminate a tenancy for personal cultivation had to give notice and apply to the Mamlatdar, and a successor-in-title to a widow had to act within one year after her interest ended. Sections 32 and 32F governed tenants’ deemed purchase rights and the timing of those rights where the landlord was a widow. The statutory scheme therefore required the successor to follow the Section 31 process; no earlier cases were relied upon.

rule.if: successor_landlord_possession_proceeding and widow_leased_land and successor_sought_personal_cultivation and tenant_holds_as_leaseholder and successor_gave_no_timely_notice and successor_made_no_timely_application

predicates.successor_landlord_possession_proceeding: The proceeding is a successor-landlord’s claim to recover leased agricultural land from a tenant after a widow-landlord’s interest has ended.
predicates.widow_leased_land: A widow-landlord leased the land to the tenant while she held an interest in it.
predicates.successor_sought_personal_cultivation: The successor sought to recover the land for personal cultivation.
predicates.tenant_holds_as_leaseholder: The defendant held the land as a tenant under a lease granted by the widow.
predicates.successor_gave_no_timely_notice: The successor did not give the tenant notice terminating the tenancy within the applicable period after the widow’s interest ended.
predicates.successor_made_no_timely_application: The successor did not apply to the tenancy authority for possession within the applicable period after the widow’s interest ended.

issues.definition: When a successor-landlord seeks leased land for personal cultivation from a tenant after a widow’s interest ends, but gives no timely notice and makes no timely application, the successor cannot recover possession under the tenancy law.
